title: Marriage Really Matters
author: Danielle Treweek
summary: Treweek critiques theological language about marriage that, though laden with Christian buzzwords, obscures biblical teaching. A viral clip describing marriage as walking to death and as a covenant made only with God misrepresents Scripture. Marriage wasn't instituted to require sacrifice—it predates sin—and Scripture presents it as an interpersonal covenant between two people witnessed by God, not two separate vertical covenants through God. Misdescribing marriage doesn't merely misuse buzzwords but obscures its true purpose: marriage is a created gift designed as a foretaste of Christ's covenant with the church, not a crucifixion.
points: Marriage was instituted in the Garden before sin existed; it belongs to creation, not redemption, so sacrifice is not its nature.
Scripture presents marriage as a bilateral covenant between man and woman, with God as witness; not three separate covenants.
The cross redeems sinners so they might learn to love within marriage; it does not define marriage itself.
Christianese can carry readers away from rigorous theology when not examined against Scripture.
Misdescribing marriage also distorts theology of atonement and discipleship, making doctrinal accuracy essential.
quotes: Scripture does not present marriage as a journey toward death but as a signpost toward life.
Human marriage itself was never designed to be a crucifixion. It was designed to be a foretaste of the wedding feast yet to come.” “Getting this right matters. It matters because marriage matters.
The cross does not define the creation ordinance of marriage itself.” Archived from Dani | Writes on April 21, 2026 by Tim.
